title: IXDE attempt with hunting predators on fuel-driven condensate prey: from noise, prey and predator populations cycle with a lag in a 256^2 arena (two seeds), predators divide after meals (19 persistent splits per seed, generation 2-3), predation turns a static prey emulsion into cycling prey, and prey bodies, whose matter is never made from fuel, dissolve when the fuel is cut
summary: world.py: prey are Cahn-Hilliard bodies of a conserved material that is miscible unless drawn up its own catalysis product, which needs a consumed, regrowing fuel (20261026T1851-c46-driven-prey-fuel-fork); predators are Cahn-Hilliard droplets that eat prey material cooperatively (k2 c_a^2 c_b^2), decay to waste that is remade into prey material everywhere (closed material ledger), and drift down the fuel gradient toward the prey that consume it (nonreciprocal taxis chiF 0.5). Prey bodies form from smoothed noise; predator material is added as smoothed noise over the whole domain at t=2000. Labkit at 256^2 (seeds 2 and 3, t=12000, --lineage-k 5): prey 57/58 -> 12/25 -> 61/51 -> 10/27 and predators 0 -> 60/61 -> 34-49/41-61 -> 45/27 cycle with a lag (pack256/seed*/timeseries.png); predators that have eaten elongate into rods and Y-shapes that pinch into separate droplets: 19 and 19 persistent predator splits (generation 2 and 3; 21 and 20 by the strict test splits3.py, 14 and 13 of them away from prey). The matched predator-free twin (twin256/seed2) is a static prey emulsion growing to 75 bodies. Cutting the fuel at t=6000 (efork/, 128^2, seeds 0 and 1) dissolves every prey body within 500-1000 t while the prey material stays in solution.

claims.statement: In pack256/seed2 and pack256/seed3 (python -m labkit.run world.py --seeds <s> --size 256 256 --frames 120 --lineage-k 5 --no-movie, defaults), prey condensates form from noise and predator droplets form on them from predator noise added at t=2000; the predators eat the prey, hunt them down the fuel gradient, and divide after meals (19 persistent splits on each seed, generation 2 and 3); the two populations cycle with a lag to t=12000 instead of the static, growing emulsion of the predator-free twin; the prey's bodies depend on the fuel flux, not on fuel-made matter (efork: every prey body dissolves after a fuel cut, material kept), and the predators are made only from prey material.
claims.track: seed 2 (pack256/seed2): the predator population that eats the 57 prey down to 12 by t=4000, falls to 34 while the prey regrow to 61, and from t~7500 splits after meals (pack256/seed2/strict_1.png: rods pinching at t=7300-8000, Y-shapes breaking at t=7600-9600; lineage.png generation 2)

controls_run.X: twin256/seed2 (pred_on 0, same seed, grid, duration and lineage window): static prey emulsion, 56 -> 75 bodies, no cycles; with predators the prey fall to 12/25 and recover to 61/51 (pack256/seed*/metrics.json species n_comp)
controls_run.E: efork/s0 and efork/s1 (fork_t 6000: F set to 0 and its regrowth kF 0) vs the fed twins run alongside (drive.py counts): prey 14 -> 0 by t=6500 and 13 -> 0 by t=7000 (fed: 4 and 15 at t=7000; on seed 0 the fed prey are also being eaten), mean prey material 0.209 -> 0.205 and 0.239 -> 0.239; predator-free forks in 20261026T1851-c46-driven-prey-fuel-fork

limits: Prey reproduce rarely in the presence of predators: 2 persistent prey splits per 256^2 seed (strict test 1 and 0), against 13 in the predator-free twin, so D for the prey kind is thin; most new prey appear by nucleation from the bath, which the predators' waste refills. Predators are added as noise at t=2000, not at t=0 (from t=0 they die before prey form). Predator E holds by construction (made only from prey material) and predators survive a fuel cut by eating the dissolved prey; the dynamical E is the prey's. The taxis is a written nonreciprocal drift of predator material toward low fuel. Predators dim between meals (threshold c_b 0.5), so their tracks are short and labkit finds no persistent tracks. No dt/2 or grid variant; fork at 128^2 with drive.py counts, not labkit.
